newsitem.title: USA: Liability tiff holds up US oil shale reserve plan.
newsitem.headline: Liability tiff holds up US oil shale reserve plan.

text.p: A U.S. Energy Department plan to transfer its naval oil shale reserves to the Interior Department depends on the two departments agreeing on who should fund future cleanup costs at the sites, a senior Energy Department official said Wednesday.

In a recent report to Congress, the Energy Department recommended transferring its three oil shale reserves to the Interior Department to lease the land out for oil and gas drilling, instead of selling off the land.

The Energy Department plans to submit legislation to carry out the proposal as soon as the two agencies decide who should be liable for potential future environmental cleanup costs, assistant energy secretary Patricia Fry Godley said Wednesday.
"That's the sticking point right now," she told reporters, after a House subcommittee hearing on the Energy Department's fossil energy budget.
Godley said she expected the issue to be resolved soon.
There are no environmental problems at the three sites at the moment, with two of the reserves largely undeveloped.
However, the Energy Department spent $3 million cleaning up a spent shale pile that had been left by a Bureau of Mines project at Naval Oil Shale Reserve No. 3 in Colorado
"The Department of Interior raised concern about who would fund any future cleanup requirements," Godley said.
